## The problem

Our team of twelve currently develops on long-lived feature branches, some open for two to four weeks before merging. This has real costs. Merges routinely produce conflicts that eat half a day or more to resolve. Integration bugs surface late, often days after the code that caused them was written, when the context has gone cold. Two engineers have independently told me they avoid refactoring shared code because they don't want to "own" the merge pain that follows. Our last release was delayed six days specifically because three branches touching the same billing module had drifted apart and had to be reconciled by hand. We are paying a steady tax in coordination overhead for a workflow that was supposed to give us isolation and safety.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: small, frequent commits merged directly to main, gated by feature flags for anything not ready for users. Concretely:

- All branches live no more than one to two days before merging to main.
- Incomplete features ship behind flags rather than staying unmerged.
- CI must pass on every merge to main, with a fast (under 10 minute) build.
- We adopt pair or mob programming for genuinely risky changes instead of isolating them on branches.
- We run a two-week pilot with one squad before rolling out team-wide.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is that trunk-based development assumes strong CI and disciplined test coverage we don't fully have yet. If our test suite has gaps, merging small, frequent, unfinished changes to main could destabilize it constantly rather than occasionally, which is worse than periodic large merges. That's a fair concern, not a straw man: our coverage is uneven in the payments and reporting modules specifically. I don't think this is a reason to abandon the proposal, but it is a reason to sequence it — we should shore up CI reliability in those two modules before or during the pilot, not after. A second risk is that feature flags accumulate as permanent clutter if we don't schedule their removal.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
